data.cultural_impact: Dushyanta is best known as the legendary king and the father of Emperor Shantanu, whose tale is featured in Mahabharata. His story symbolizes the power of love and self-discipline to purify one's mind and soul.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dushyanta represents an individual's ongoing internal battle against temptation and negativity. It serves as a reminder that even those with wicked tendencies can harness their inner strength and control to lead a virtuous and enlightened life.

historical_references.reference: Rigveda X.61.3 mentions a king named Dushyanta, who was the father of Shakuntala and the legendary emperor Bharata.
historical_references.context: Rigveda is one of the oldest existing texts in Hinduism, consisting of hymns and prayers to various deities. This reference suggests that Dushyanta was a prominent king during this period.

historical_references.reference: Mahabharata Adi Parva, Section 107, describes Dushyanta as the sage Vena's son who ruled over Hastinapura with his wife Shakuntala.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an epic poem that forms a major part of Hindu literature. This reference places Dushyanta's rule during this time period.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Dushyanta is a significant figure in Indian mythology and ancient history. He is known as the legendary king of Hastinapura, the capital city of the Pandavas in the epic Mahabharata. Dushyanta is also remembered for his unique connection to the goddess Shakuntala, with whom he fathered the great hero Bhagavad-Gita narrator, King Yudhishthira. Today, Dushyanta's story is popularized on various digital platforms, including Twitter through user-generated content and discussions around literature and mythology, Instagram with visually appealing content showcasing artwork and depictions of the character, and YouTube through educational and philosophical videos that delve into the deeper meanings and teachings behind the legend.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Maya Dushyanta in Bali, Indonesia attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Dushyanta, which means "Warrior from heaven". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Dushyanta, meaning 'tormented by desire', signifies the intense longing and passion for love, symbolic of Lord Rama's pursuit for Sita. It's a reminder of the power of deep, unwavering love that can conquer all obstacles.
